title: Repaying Bix; Bix's last days and death
summary: Later he lends Bix $125 at Jimmy Plunkett's; Bix soon dies of pneumonia.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Well no, the top priced men of the band like Benny Goodman was, and Teagarden and myself. We were you know, like stars of the band. And we made plenty of money so I paid Bix back and everything was fine. Now we are coming to the Jimmy Plunket's, the speak easy. I'm now finished with Pollack's band, I'm working in a show called 'Sons of Guns' with Jack Donahue and Lilly Damita and I'm in the pit and I'm making $250 a week in the pit there and working
in pictures at Paramount Studios and making recordings, so I was probably making close to $500 a week.

Now in 1930, '31 this is a lot of money. And no taxes or anything like that. So Jimmy Murphy's, not Jimmy Murphy's, Jimmy Plunkett's speak easy, I went over there one afternoon and Jimmy Dorsey, he and I, we were babies, so Bix is there and he's got a bad cold, a very bad cold. And he's not feeling well. He said to me, he says kid, have you got any money? I said, sure, I said what do you need? So I went in my pocket and said do you remember the time you gave me two hundred? I went in my pocket, my wallet and I came out and I had one hundred and thirty dollars. I said, here's a hundred and twenty five you know.

He said, beautiful, great he said, I'm working down at Princeton University in a couple of days and I'll pay you back. I said, don't worry about it, the same as you told me, you know. You pay it back when you, when you've got it. I don't need it. I'm working and making plenty of money. So he said, okay kid, thanks, you know. And that was the last time I saw him alive.
This bad cold that he had at this time and he
drank so much you know that he went down to Princeton and played this job down there and it developed into pneumonia and he died, of pneumonia.
And those were the days when pneumonia was really fatal. The percentage of fatalities was very high.
That's very true. But that's the kind of guys we were in those days you know. You needed something each musician to a musician you helped each other out.
You really understood something about what friendship was all about.
You sure did. Boy, when you're not eating and you need money and nobody will give you any money you'll find out who your friend is real quick. Real quick, rather.
